Key Takeaways
  • Ahaan Panday's debut film grossed over 579 crore, becoming the highest-grossing Indian romantic film.
  • Lakshya transitions from action to romance with 'Chand Mera Dil', set for OTT release on JioHotstar.
  • New Bollywood heroes emphasize vulnerability and emotional intelligence over traditional machismo.
  • Filmfare highlights 28 new romantic pairings for 2026, focusing on emotionally driven narratives.
  • These characters resonate with the Indian diaspora, offering relatable emotional experiences.

A new generation of leading men is reshaping what it means to be a romantic hero in Bollywood. From Ahaan Panday’s record-shattering debut in Saiyaara to Lakshya’s earnest turn in Chand Mera Dil, the young actors headlining Hindi cinema’s love stories in 2025-2026 are trading the chest-thumping machismo of past eras for vulnerability, emotional intelligence, and a quiet sincerity that audiences worldwide are embracing.

Ahaan Panday: The Breakout Star

Panday’s debut film Saiyaara, directed by Mohit Suri and produced by Yash Raj Films, did not merely succeed at the box office — it rewrote the record books. The musical romantic drama grossed over 579 crore worldwide, surpassing Kabir Singh to become the highest-grossing Indian romantic film of all time. In an age where action franchises and superhero spectacles dominate, a love story built around a singer-songwriter duo proved that audiences still crave emotional storytelling done right.

Director Ali Abbas Zafar, who is now collaborating with Panday on an action-romance for YRF alongside Sharvari, has praised the young actor’s natural screen presence. “Audiences have connected with Ahaan because he’s not trying to impress them. He’s simply present in the moment,” Zafar said. “There’s a softness to him but also strength. That balance is what makes people root for him, especially in love stories.”

Lakshya: From Action to Aarav

Lakshya, who earned critical acclaim and a Filmfare Best Male Debut award for the brutal action film Kill (2023), made a sharp pivot with Chand Mera Dil, a Dharma Productions romantic drama that released theatrically in May 2026 and begins streaming on JioHotstar on July 17. Directed by Vivek Soni and co-starring Ananya Panday, the film follows engineering students Aarav and Chandni through the joys, heartbreaks, and hard-won maturity of young love.

“I’m thrilled that Chand Mera Dil will now reach an even wider audience on JioHotstar,” Lakshya said. “It’s the kind of story that stays with you long after the credits roll.” The film’s OTT debut is expected to find new life among diaspora viewers who may have missed its theatrical run.

What Makes Them Different

What separates this new wave from predecessors like Shah Rukh Khan’s grand gestures or Shahid Kapoor’s brooding intensity is a willingness to be openly vulnerable. These are not heroes who chase the heroine across continents or fight off armies of goons. Instead, they navigate the quieter battles — parental disapproval, financial hardship, the slow erosion of a relationship under everyday pressure. It is a shift that mirrors evolving attitudes toward masculinity among younger Indian audiences, both in India and across the global diaspora.

The New Wave of Romantic Heroes
›Focus on vulnerability over machismo
›Navigate everyday relationship challenges
›28 new romantic pairings highlighted for 2026
›Appeal to contemporary emotional landscapes

The trend extends beyond just Panday and Lakshya. Filmfare recently highlighted 28 new on-screen pairings for 2026, many of them centered on emotionally driven narratives rather than action spectacles. From Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi in Ramayana to Ram Charan and Janhvi Kapoor in Peddi, Bollywood’s slate signals that romance, reimagined for a new generation, is back at the center of Indian cinema.

For the Indian diaspora, these new romantic heroes offer something their predecessors did not always provide: characters whose emotional landscapes feel contemporary and relatable, whether you are watching in a multiplex in Mumbai or streaming on a laptop in New Jersey.
